authors: McRoberts, R.E., Stehman, S.V., Liknes, G.C., Naesset, E., Sannier, C. & Walters, B.F.
title: The effects of imperfect reference data on remote sensing-assisted estimators of land cover class proportions
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 142, 292-300
relevance: Shows that when a simple MAJORITY interpretation across experts is used as the final reference label, bias grows with unequal strata sizes, smaller maps, lower interpreter accuracy, FEWER interpreters, and - critically for us - GREATER CORRELATION AMONG INTERPRETERS. A single interpreter is the limiting case of that correlation, which is our planned design. Supplies a hybrid variance estimator for when the whole sample is interpreted by several people, and is the reason the CEOS protocol (ID 187) recommends consensus or interpenetrating designs over one expert working alone.
